titleJa: どこへ いきますか
summaryEn: Go, come and go home: say where, how (train, bus, on foot), with whom and when — and give dates.

grammar.pattern: N(place)へ いきます／きます／かえります
grammar.meaningEn: go / come / return to a place (direction particle へ, read "e")
grammar.exampleJa: あした きょうとへ いきます。
grammar.exampleEn: I am going to Kyoto tomorrow.

grammar.pattern: どこ[へ]も いきません／いきませんでした
grammar.meaningEn: not go anywhere (question word + も + negative)
grammar.exampleJa: にちようびは どこも いきませんでした。
grammar.exampleEn: I didn't go anywhere on Sunday.

grammar.pattern: N(vehicle)で いきます／あるいて いきます
grammar.meaningEn: go by a means of transport (で); on foot is あるいて with no で; なんで = by what
grammar.exampleJa: バスで いきます。えきから あるいて かえります。
grammar.exampleEn: I go by bus. I walk home from the station.

grammar.meaningEn: do something with someone (と); alone is ひとりで (no と); だれと = with whom
grammar.exampleJa: ともだちと にほんへ きました。
grammar.exampleEn: I came to Japan with a friend.

grammar.meaningEn: when? (いつ takes no に; so do きょねん, らいしゅう, あした …)
grammar.exampleJa: いつ にほんへ きましたか。…きょねん きました。
grammar.exampleEn: When did you come to Japan? — I came last year.

grammar.pattern: ～がつ ～にち／なんがつ なんにち
grammar.meaningEn: dates: month + day (ついたち, ふつか … はつか have special readings)
grammar.exampleJa: たんじょうびは 5がつ 15にちです。

grammar.meaningEn: sentence-final よ: telling the listener something they don't know
grammar.exampleJa: その でんしゃは みどりのへ いきませんよ。
grammar.exampleEn: That train doesn't go to Midorino, you know.

tipsEn: Station staff answer in very few words: 「2ばんせんです。」 Listen for the number + ばんせん (platform).
A local train (ふつう) stops everywhere; an express (きゅうこう) skips small stations. Always check which one you are boarding.
On Monday mornings colleagues often ask where you went at the weekend. 「どこも いきませんでした」 is a perfectly fine answer.

research.notesEn: Lesson 5 introduces the motion verbs いきます／きます／かえります with the direction particle へ, means of transport with で (but あるいて without で), company with と (but ひとりで), the question word いつ (no に), question word + も + negative (どこも いきません), sentence-final よ, and dates (months, days of the month, last/this/next week, month, year). Real-life fits: asking station staff which train or platform goes to your stop, small talk about when and with whom you came to Japan, Monday-morning chat about the weekend, birthdays and holiday plans. Typical mistakes: pronouncing へ as "he", adding で to あるいて, と after ひとり, に after いつ or らいしゅう, and a positive verb after どこも. The three variants are a station errand, a park-bench chat and a Monday office chat, each written from scratch with the town cast.

variants.titleJa: この でんしゃは いきますか
variants.briefEn: Saturday morning. You're off to see the cherry blossoms at Sakura Park in Midorino. A train is standing at the platform — is it yours? Ask Okada-san at the gate.
variants.roleEn: You are a traveller who is new to this line. You want to get to Midorino, then to Sakura Park.

missionsEn.text: Ask whether that train goes to Midorino
Ask how to get from Midorino Station to Sakura Park
Help another passenger: tell her about the train
Say whether you're going alone or with someone

branches.whenEn: Learner asked which platform or which train goes to Midorino, or only said that they are going to Midorino.

say.kana: さくらこうえんですか。えきから バスで いきます。
say.en: Sakura Park? You go by bus from the station.

say.kana: 3ばんの バスですよ。

say.kana: すみません。あの でんしゃは みどりのへ いきますか。
say.en: Excuse me. Does that train go to Midorino?

いいえ、いきませんよ。2ばんせんです。

branches.whenEn: Learner said yes, that train goes to Midorino.

say.kana: わたしも さくらこうえんへ いきます。

say.en: Are you going alone?

modelAnswers: いいえ、ともだちと いきます。
はい、ひとりで いきます。

branches.whenEn: Learner is going alone.

say.kana: そうですか。わたしは ひとりで いきます。
say.en: I see. I'm going by myself.

say.ja: わたしも 一人です。
say.kana: わたしも ひとりです。
say.en: I'm on my own too.

say.ja: 9時40分の 普通です。2番線へ どうぞ。
say.kana: 9じ40ぷんの ふつうです。2ばんせんへ どうぞ。
say.en: That's the 9:40 local. Platform 2, please.
say.tts: くじ よんじゅっぷんの ふつうです。にばんせんへ どうぞ。

variants.titleJa: こうえんの ベンチで
variants.titleEn: A chat on the park bench
variants.briefEn: Saturday morning under the cherry trees. Hara-san, who walks here every day, sits down on your bench — and she is curious about you.
variants.roleEn: You are yourself: answer with your real story (when you came to Japan, with whom, how you got here today).

missionsEn.text: Say when and with whom you came to Japan
Say how you came to the park today
Ask Hara-san a question about her walks
Say where you're going tomorrow — or nowhere

ことしの 1がつに きました。

say.kana: そうですか。だれと きましたか。

じてんしゃで きました。

branches.whenEn: Learner came on foot.

まいにち なんじに きますか。

branches.whenEn: Learner asked who she comes with, or whether she comes alone.
branches.exampleJa: だれと ここへ きますか。

say.ja: わたしも どこも 行きません。
say.kana: わたしも どこも いきません。

freeTalk.openerJa: お国は どちらですか。
freeTalk.openerKana: おくには どちらですか。
freeTalk.topicEn: Gentle small talk on the bench: the learner's country, when they go home, how they get to school or work, who they go with. Stay within lesson 1–5 grammar (no adjectives, no て-form).

variants.titleJa: げつようびの あさ
variants.briefEn: Monday, a few minutes before 9. Aoki-san is by the calendar and wants to hear about your weekend — and your birthday, and your summer plans.
variants.roleEn: You are Aoki-san's colleague from abroad. Answer truthfully or make it up — staying home is a fine answer too.

missionsEn.text: Say where you went at the weekend — or that you didn't go anywhere
Talk about who with and how (yours or hers)
Tell her the date of your birthday

say.kana: おはよう ございます。
